zh: 利润 2^i 有个特别的性质：它比所有下标更小的商品利润加起来还要大。所以能不能买到下标最高的那件，比后面所有商品加起来都重要。
既然利润的比较等价于从高下标往低下标的字典序比较，就从最高下标开始贪心：当前商品买得起就买，买不起就跳过，再看下一个更低的下标。
预处理 2^i 对 10^9+7 取模的值；剩余资金 rem 初始为 x（需要 64 位，最大 10^14）；下标从 n−1 递减到 0，若 cost[i] ≤ rem，就从 rem 中扣掉 cost[i] 并把 2^i 的模值累加进答案；比较时只用真实的成本和资金，不要拿取模后的利润做比较；最后输出答案。
en: The profit 2^i has a special property: it is larger than the combined profit of all items with smaller indices. So whether you can afford the highest-index item matters more than everything below it put together.

Since comparing profits is the same as comparing the chosen index sets lexicographically from high index to low, go greedily from the highest index: buy the current item if you can afford it, otherwise skip it and move to the next lower index.

Precompute 2^i modulo 10^9+7; keep the remaining money rem starting at x (use 64 bits, it can reach 10^14); for i from n-1 down to 0, if cost[i] <= rem, subtract cost[i] from rem and add the modded 2^i to the answer; compare only real costs and money, never profits after the modulo; print the answer.

explanationEn:
## Problem

There are n items; item i (0-based) costs cost[i] and resells for a profit of 2^i. With total money x, each item can be bought at most once and the total cost may not exceed x. Find the maximum profit modulo 10^9+7.

## Approach

2^i is larger than the sum of all profits at smaller indices (2^0+...+2^(i-1)=2^i-1), so comparing profits is equivalent to comparing the chosen sets lexicographically from the highest index down. Go greedily from the highest index downwards: if the current item's cost does not exceed the remaining money, buy it and subtract its cost. Take the modulo when adding 2^i.

## Correctness

Let i be the first index where the greedy differs from some optimal solution. If the greedy bought i and the optimal solution did not, the greedy gains an extra 2^i at i, which exceeds everything the optimal solution earns at lower indices, a contradiction. If the greedy did not buy i, then buying i together with the already chosen higher indices exceeds the budget; the optimal solution agrees with the greedy on the higher indices, so it cannot buy i either. Hence the greedy is optimal. All comparisons use the structure of the real profits rather than modded values; the modulo is applied only while accumulating.

## Complexity

O(n). The money can reach 10^14, so use 64-bit integers.

## Independent verification

The oracle enumerates all subsets, computes the real profit with Python big integers, takes the maximum and then the modulo (small data only), without using the greedy. Every combination with n=1..5, costs 1..3 and x=1..7 was enumerated and the reference program was actually run on each. The wrong solutions cover greedy from low indices, not buying when the cost exactly equals the remaining money, missing the modulo, and 32-bit money.
